title: E1 — Graph store core — 3 types, one file, fold
description:
The substrate. Everything blocks on this and nothing in it is optional.

**There is one file.** §0.5 deleted the derived snapshot; §0.6 deleted `blobs/`, `plan/` and `schema.json`. Every read folds `mutations.jsonl`.

**Gate:** folding the same log twice yields an identical graph; a torn final line is tolerated.

title: T1.2 — packages/core — 2 node types, 1 edge kind, 5 statuses
description:
**2 node types** — `task`, and `wait` with three match kinds (`event` · `human` · `predicate`, the last being what used to be `quorum`). **1 edge kind** — `blocks` with an optional `condition`; §0.8 deleted `supersedes` and `compensates` because both were already node fields, represented twice. **Edge record is `{from, to, condition?}` — no identity.** **5 statuses** (`active|sending|done|failed|dropped`). `status`/`outcome`/`output`, typed deadlines in 3 shapes.

Collapsing `quorum` into `wait` gave it a **mandatory deadline it never had**, closing the liveness hole where a quorum with no clock hangs forever.

Recorded tension: **the store knows two types; the authoring prompt may still say more words.**

**Zero dependencies — this unblocks W3 and W4.**

title: E2 — Mutation engine — 6 ops, 3 invariants, CAS
description:
The code that stands between the LLM and the file. Builds a candidate graph in memory, checks the invariants, and only then touches disk — so a bad batch is never half-applied.

Cut to 6 ops by §0.5, 3 invariants by §0.7; §0.6 cut the taxonomy underneath. T2.6 is never-cut.

title: T2.1 — The 6 ops — apply functions, fixed internal order
description:
add_node · add_edge · set_status · record_outcome · record_output · supersede_node.

Internal order: additions and rewires BEFORE cancellations (Zeebe). A batch violating that order is rejected, never silently reordered.

**§0.5 deleted five ops** — `fan_out`, `add_wait`, `insert_compensation`, `reroute_edge`, `resolve_gate`. All five were `add_node`/`add_edge` with sugar: **the atomic unit is the commit, not the op**, so a batch already gives the all-or-nothing guarantee `fan_out` existed to provide. That also deletes the auto-wiring table (old T2.3), which caused every orphan in the v2 probe.

No `delete_node`. No `rollback` opcode, not even reserved.

title: T2.4 — The 3 enforced invariants + parser + CAS check
description:
**A zod parser first, free:** legal type + required fields, legal edge kind, a `condition` on every wait out-edge, and every wait having a deadline + `on_timeout`. Those are *shape*, not graph properties.

**Then three invariants:**
1 terminal & effect protection — an **op-delta** predicate against pre-commit head state
2 predicate-waits stay satisfiable (what `quorum` used to be)
3 **effects are bounded and addressed** — (a) cumulative sends ≤ the approved budget; (b) `recipient_ref` resolves to an evidenced entity. §0.7 merged these: both answer *may this effect exist?* at the same moment. Clause (b) is what stops the mutator inventing people to email

Plus CAS on `parent_v`. **#1 is op-delta, not a post-state scan** — as a state predicate it rejected every commit once any node reached `done`.

Stryker target: 100.

---

notes:
PARTIAL after slice 1. DONE: zod parser, invariant 1 (op-delta vs pre-commit head), role authority, CAS.

REMAINING — and one of the two has a spec gap:

INVARIANT 2 (predicate-waits stay satisfiable). Needs NO new types: population is the wait blocking in-edges, and it reads status.outcome.verdict / status.outcome.attrs, which exist. `satisfiable iff matching_confirmed + still_live >= n`. Note "still_live" must use the SAME notion of live as T2.6 branch resolution — a dropped source neither satisfies nor blocks. Build them together or agree the predicate first.

INVARIANT 3(b) recipient-evidence — highest-value check in the codebase, and it needs no new types either. At n=60 the mutator met an unsatisfiable predicate by INVENTING counterparties and queueing email to them, passing every other check. A recipient existing only in the proposing batch is rejected.

INVARIANT 3(a) — SPEC GAP, do not invent silently. "cumulative irreversible sends <= the approved budget" appears in spec §6.7 and §6.9 but the budget is DEFINED NOWHERE: no op sets it, and §6.1 gives .kona/ exactly two files (mutations.jsonl, lock) with no room for config. Options are (i) a field on the genesis record, (ii) a new op, (iii) a per-node cap like max_reattempts, (iv) drop 3(a) and keep only 3(b). Raise it with Ilya rather than picking one. 3(b) is independently shippable and is the half the probe evidence actually demands.

Seam: packages/core/src/validate.ts only. Slice 1 left checkInvariant1 as a standalone exported function specifically so 2 and 3 can be added beside it without touching validate().

title: T2.6 — Branch resolution — store drops untaken branches
description:
**NEVER CUT.** On terminal resolution the store marks untaken branch targets `dropped`, transitively, stopping at any node still held by a live blocking in-edge. An in-edge whose SOURCE is dropped is excluded from merge evaluation.

Readiness fails safe and does NOT inherit the exclusion — otherwise the second node on an untaken branch has no blocker, lands on the frontier, and gets dispatched.

Without this, v2's dominant silent deadlock returns.

---
**Effort:** 3h / 45m · **Epic:** E2 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T2.6
notes:
DESIGN DECISION, settle before writing code.

Branch resolution must EXPAND INTO EXPLICIT OPS AT COMMIT TIME. It must NOT run as an implicit cascade inside applyOps().

Why: fold() replays every record through applyOps (packages/core/src/fold.ts:105). A cascade living inside applyOps therefore re-runs on EVERY fold, forever, using whatever the code does TODAY. Change the drop rule in a month and every historical log folds to a different graph than the one the human approved. That breaks D1 (resurrection) and it breaks it silently — the log is unchanged, so nothing looks wrong.

Same principle already settled for id minting: the store decides ONCE, at commit, and the log records the decision. `kona mutate` normalizes the batch (refs resolved, ids minted) and writes the COMMITTED form; fold is a dumb replay that mints nothing and derives nothing. Branch drops belong in exactly that category.

So: when a wait resolves, `mutate` appends the derived `set_status(..., dropped)` ops to the batch it is about to commit, and the rationale explains them. The drops become visible in the log, diffable in the viewer, and stable under code change.

Seam: this is packages/core (a pure function computing the drop set) plus one call site in packages/kona/src/commands/mutate.ts. Coordinate on the mutate.ts line only.

Spec: §6.4 branch resolution. Readiness FAILS SAFE and does not inherit the merge exclusion — a dropped source never satisfies readiness, or the second node on an untaken branch lands on the frontier and gets dispatched, pivot send included.

title: T2.7 — O_EXCL lockfile (portable) + compare-and-swap
description:
**An `O_EXCL` lockfile, not `flock`.** `fs.open(path,'wx')` fails atomically if the file exists, on macOS, Linux and Windows alike; `flock` is POSIX-only and Windows has no equivalent. Same amount of code — write the portable one first.

Store `{pid, started_at}` in the lock and treat one older than the longest legal write as stale.

Then compare-and-swap: `--base-version` must equal head, else **exit 3 + `STALE_BASE_VERSION` + the current head**. Re-read and re-decide, never blind-merge.

*(54 cross-actor overwrites in Beads' data were median 31 minutes apart — the enemy is hand-offs, not races, so the fix is rejection.)*

---

close_reason: O_EXCL lockfile with {pid, started_at}. Stale reclaim is by RENAME, not unlink-then-create: the latter is not atomic across two reclaimers and both would have believed they held it. CAS is checked INSIDE the lock, since folding before locking validates against a head another writer can move.

title: T3.1 — Wait schema — or-group conditions, deadline evaluation
description:
First-wins or-group. `deadline` non-nullable, `on_timeout` required. Four-way resolution `satisfied|timeout|bounced|dropped`. `last_checked_at` so the viewer can tell patient from stuck.

**One type, three match kinds** (§0.7): `{kind:"event"}` an inbound reply · `{kind:"human"}` a decision · `{kind:"predicate"}` a condition over its own blocking in-edges — what `quorum` used to be, and it now inherits the mandatory deadline.

Matching is deterministic: plus-tag, then `In-Reply-To`. **A model classifies the reply's *intent*; `kona` never decides whether an event happened.**

Plus the three states retry never converged on: late reply, tentative, quorum-met bulk.

title: E4 — CLI surface — 9 verbs, brief, and ZERO model calls
description:
The one interface every other block builds against. Nothing outside the CLI reads or writes `.kona/`.

**⚖ THE LAW (§6.8.2): the `kona` binary never calls a language model.** Every verb is a pure function of `mutations.jsonl` + the clock + the mailbox cursor. Judgment lives entirely in the plugin.

Four consequences: the store is testable to 100% (nothing stochastic to mock); crash-resume is decidable rather than plausible; cost is bounded by events rather than turns; and it is the honest positioning — **Kona is Beads with state machines, plus the plugin Beads never had.**

`lint` and `plan`/`apply` were deleted by §0.5.

title: T4.1 handoff — kona view wires @kona/viewer's serveViewer()
description:
**E6 built the server; E4 owns the verb.** `packages/viewer` exports it so `kona view` stays
three lines and the seam holds — the viewer never imports `@kona/cli`, and `kona` gains a
dependency on `@kona/viewer` rather than the other way round.

```ts
import { serveViewer } from "@kona/viewer";
const served = await serveViewer({ root, port });   // { url, stop }
```

- Binds `127.0.0.1` by default, never `0.0.0.0` (§6.10 rule 9: a pursuit log carries
  counterparty names and message ids).
- Default port 4747.
- Routes: `GET /api/log` (raw bytes), `GET /api/events` (SSE, whole log per message,
  debounced `fs.watch`), everything else the bundled front end. **No route writes anything.**
- `kona view` is user-run, never plugin-spawned (§6.8).

The verb needs: `--port`, resolving the pursuit root the way the other verbs do, printing the
URL, and holding the process until `SIGINT` → `served.stop()`.

title: Readability at 97 nodes — T6.4's cut rationale does not survive 31 arms
description:
**Plan §9's second known unknown, answered by looking — and the answer is not the one §0.5
assumed.**

T6.4 (group collapse) was deleted with the reasoning "**six arms are readable flat**". That was
true of a six-arm fan-out. The PRD scopes a pursuit as "email up to **30** players from this
roster", and at that size it is not.

Measured against a 97-node pursuit built by the real binary (31 arms of `ask → wait → thank`,
plus four setup nodes; generated over five versions so the tween runs at scale):

| | |
|---|---|
| graph extent | **1328 x 5216 px** — 4 ranks wide, 31 arms tall |
| canvas pane | 1131 x 672 px |
| zoom to fit the whole thing | **0.13** — a 260px card renders at **34px** |
| what that looks like | not a small graph; a grey smear |
| legibility floor | ~**0.45**, where a card is 117px and its label is readable |
| what fits at 0.45 | about **10 of 31 arms** |

`kona graph --json` and the fold are fine at this size — 97 nodes and 95 edges, page load 577ms,
dagre memoised so a status tick still moves nothing.

**Shipped now:** `fitView` gained a legibility floor (`minZoom: 0.45`), so the opening shot is
as much of the graph as stays readable rather than an unreadable whole; the canvas `minZoom`
dropped to 0.05 so deliberately zooming out to see the SHAPE of a fan-out is still possible.
The minimap carries status colour, which is what makes the zoomed-out view worth having.

**Not shipped, and this is the ask:** at 31 arms the reader scrolls through ten screens of
near-identical cards. Every arm already carries `provenance.group` — the fixture and this
stress pursuit both set `scope` per counterparty — so the data for a container per group is
already in the log. §6.10 rule 3 asked for exactly this ("collapse fan-out groups by default —
one container, aggregate status, edges redirected to it") and it was cut on a six-arm premise.

**Reopen T6.4 if the demo pursuit has more than about ten arms.** Below that, flat is fine and
the cut still holds.

Regenerate the stress pursuit: `scripts/` has no copy — it was built from a throwaway generator.
Worth committing one if T6.4 is picked up.

title: Spec gap — rule 10's read contract cannot feed rule 5's timeline panel
description:
**§6.10 rule 10 says `kona graph --json` + file-watch is the one read contract. Rule 5 asks
for a panel that contract cannot feed.**

`GraphProjection` carries `{schema_version, version, nodes, edges}`. It does not carry `v`,
`ops`, `rationale.why`, `reason_code`, `actor` or `trigger`. So a viewer built strictly on
rule 10 can render the canvas and *nothing else the spec asks for*:

- rule 5, the mutation timeline — version + op + rationale. Called out as the differentiator.
- rule 6, read-only time travel — needs every version, not head.
- rule 4's deadline countdown for a `{after, duration}` deadline — the anchor's completion
  instant is `records[observed_at_version].observed_at`, which the projection drops.

**Resolved in E6 by folding the log in the viewer, not by adding a verb.** The viewer reads
the same one file and folds it with `@kona/core`'s own `foldLog`/`projectGraph` — the exact
functions `kona graph --json` calls — so it cannot drift, and it still never imports
`@kona/cli`. `packages/viewer/test/contract.test.ts` asserts
`projectGraph(foldLog(log).graph)` deep-equals `fixtures/thursday.graph.json` including key
order, which turns the prose rule into a check.

This is why §6.12 gives `viewer` a dependency on `core` at all; the spec text just never
followed through. **The spec wording should say so**: the read contract is the log plus
core's fold, and `kona graph --json` is that same fold projected for a shell.

The alternative — a second verb, or `graph --json --with-log` — was rejected: pass three
deleted three verbs for wrapping `graph`, and a second server-side projection is a second
thing that can disagree with the first.

title: goalie-confirmed is permanently unreachable until T2.6 lands
description:
**Found by the viewer, at head, on the committed fixture — and it is not a viewer bug.**

`goalie-confirmed` has five in-edges. One of them is `wait-for-priya`, which v7 dropped after
her address bounced 550. `satisfiesBlockingEdge` is `state === "done"` and nothing else, and
`isReady` requires **every** in-edge satisfied, so:

```
isEdgeSatisfied(wait-for-priya -> goalie-confirmed) = false, permanently
isReady(goalie-confirmed)                          = false, permanently
readyFrontier(graph)                               excludes it, for ever
```

`kona next` will never list the node the whole pursuit converges on, whatever Marcus or Pat
answer. The viewer renders that honestly — `blockedReason.unreachable` is true and the card
carries `⛌` — because `unreachable` is `causes.some(isPermanent)`: one permanently dead
in-edge is already fatal under an all-edges rule.

**The store is what changes, not the view.** §6.4 also says the store *drops untaken branches
transitively* and that a **dropped source is excluded from a merge** — that is T2.6, branch
resolution, which is not built. Once it lands, `wait-for-priya` stops being an unsatisfied
blocking edge rather than staying one for ever.

Two things worth knowing while it is open:

- **`spec.merge` is parsed and never read.** `MERGE_MODES` is in the schema; grep `core` and
  nothing consults it — `isReady` least of all. So `merge:"any"` is currently indistinguishable
  from `merge:"all"`, and the viewer deliberately does NOT implement the `any` semantics: it
  would be rendering a rule the store does not have.
- **The fixture is a good test case exactly because of this.** Do not "fix" it by un-dropping
  Priya; the four-arm fan-out with a dead arm is what makes T2.6 testable.
